\chapter{Clothes and Expensive: One Dot Below}
\label{ch:mw-shopping-seven}
\hlchaptermodality{20}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can add clothes and expensive to the shopping map after learning only the nukta that changes \mw{ड} to \mw{ड़}.}

Two source-attested shopping words begin by ear, add one dotted consonant, and join the earlier five words in four separately scored skills.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[kapṛā]{Hear \emph{kapṛā} — clothes}

\label{lesson:MW-C15-hear-kapda}



\begin{quote}
Recall the five-word shopping map.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{What to know first}
\begin{quote}
\emph{kapṛā} — \textbf{clothes; cloth}
\end{quote}

Listen for the quick curled sound in the middle. Say the word once from a clothes cue. Keep the written form covered for now.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://www.marwaripathshala.com/marwari-lesson-9-english}{Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 9}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[nukta]{\mw{ड़} — one dot under familiar \mw{ड}}

\label{lesson:MW-W15-nukta}



\begin{quote}
Say clothes, then write familiar \textbf{\mw{ड}}, paternal grandmother, and goods.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Script — one mark}
\begin{quote}
\textbf{\mw{ड}} + \textbf{\mw{़}} $\to$ \textbf{\mw{ड़}}
\end{quote}

The dot below is called a nukta. Here it marks the quick curled sound in \emph{kapṛā}.

\subsection*{Your turn}
Trace \textbf{\mw{ड़}} once. Copy it once. Cover it, wait five seconds, and write \textbf{\mw{ड़}} from the sound cue.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://www.unicode.org/charts/PDF/U0900.pdf}{Unicode Devanagari chart}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[kapṛā]{\mw{कपड़ा} — clothes on the page}

\label{lesson:MW-C15-kapda}



\begin{quote}
Say clothes and family, then write \textbf{\mw{ड़}}.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{What to know first}
\begin{quote}
\textbf{\mw{कप}} + \textbf{\mw{ड़ा}} $\to$ \textbf{\mw{कपड़ा}} — \emph{kapṛā} — clothes
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Look, cover, wait five seconds, and write \textbf{\mw{कपड़ा}}. Check the dot below \textbf{\mw{ड}}.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://www.marwaripathshala.com/marwari-lesson-9-english}{Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 9}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[mahaṅgo]{Hear \emph{mahaṅgo} — expensive}

\label{lesson:MW-C15-hear-mahango}



\begin{quote}
Say cheap and clothes, then write \textbf{\mw{व}}.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{What to know first}
\begin{quote}
\emph{mahaṅgo} — \textbf{expensive}
\end{quote}

Hear the price contrast: \emph{sastā} is cheap; \emph{mahaṅgo} is expensive. Say only the word that matches a high-price cue.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://www.marwaripathshala.com/marwari-lesson-9-english}{Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 9}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[mahaṅgo]{\mw{महंगो} — expensive on the page}

\label{lesson:MW-C15-mahango}



\begin{quote}
Say expensive, write cheap and family, then write short \textbf{\mw{ु}}.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{What to know first}
\begin{quote}
\textbf{\mw{महं}} + \textbf{\mw{गो}} $\to$ \textbf{\mw{महंगो}} — \emph{mahaṅgo} — expensive
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Look, cover, wait five seconds, and write \textbf{\mw{महंगो}}. Check \textbf{\mw{ं}} above and \textbf{\mw{ो}} around the final \textbf{\mw{ग}}.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://www.marwaripathshala.com/marwari-lesson-9-english}{Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 9}.
\end{tcolorbox}
